title: Latency-led geo stewardship with dynamic capacity honoring
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and implement a multi-region routing policy that prioritizes meeting latency SLOs while respecting regional capacity signals. The feature combines latency-based routing (quantile-driven decisions), soft geo-pinning for warm-state locality, and capacity-aware steering that uses per-region capacity hints + tokenized shedding. We will integrate this with circuit breakers for degraded regions and add observability and rollback controls in the Console.
acceptance_criteria: Routing selects preferred region for >95% of requests when local p95 < target and sufficient capacity hints present
Traffic gracefully fails over to secondary regions within target latency SLA when local region circuit breaker trips
Token shedding reduces low-priority requests under sustained capacity pressure without increasing p95 above SLO for high-priority routes
Metrics for per-region selected_rate, failover_rate, shed_rate, and effective_p95 are emitted and surfaced in Console
Canary rollout plan validated on internal customer workload with emergency rollback guardrails
tasks: Finalize routing policy DSL and config knobs (latency thresholds, pinning decay, capacity weight)
Implement capacity hint protocol between allocator + regional agents
Add circuit breaker state machine hook to routing layer (open/half-open/closed)
Implement tokenized shedding strategy and priority buckets
Wire telemetry: sampling, histograms, and per-route region attribution
End-to-end integration tests and chaos tests (region fail, spike, delayed responses)
Docs and Console dashboard: per-route region breakdown and SLO heatmap
Prepare rollout runbook and canary gates
comments: 2025-01-11 Ava Chen: Kickoff design review completed. Agreed on p95 as main SLO signal and p99 for safety fences. Need to define 'sufficient capacity' metric (suggest tokens_available > 20% of average) and pinning decay window.

2025-01-20 Martin Alvarez: Prototype capacity hint protocol implemented (allocator -> region-agent heartbeat + tokens_available). Simulated 10k rps test shows 12% reduction in cross-region KV misses with pinning enabled.

2025-01-28 Design feedback (R. Singh): Recommend adding an explicit low-priority request class for shedding (analytics/telemetry) and ensure rate limits apply before shedding to protect control plane.

2025-02-02 QA: Chaos test—simulated regional outage. Routing successfully tripped circuit breaker and shifted 100% of traffic within 1.2s, p95 stabilized in secondary region after warmup. Observed increased error budget for some edge routes; created ENG-904322 to harden cold-start penalties.
2025-02-04 Security review: No secrets introduced. Confirmed compliance with existing KMS policies. Minor request to log circuit-breaker transitions to audit trail (added to tasks).
telemetry_queries: SELECT region, percentile_latency(p95) FROM request_spans WHERE route = :route GROUP BY region
implementation_notes: Latency decision uses moving-window quantiles (sliding 1m, 5m, 1h) with hysteresis to avoid flapping
Pinning uses soft affinity with exponential decay (half-life: 10 minutes) and immediate prewarming hints for cached KV
Capacity hints are token buckets emitted by regional allocator; tokens map to concurrent request budget and are weighted by model instance sizes
Circuit breaker opens when regional p99 > SLO*2 for >30s or error_rate > 5% for >60s; half-open tries 1% of baseline traffic
Tokenized shedding prioritizes requests by label: high (interactive), medium (batch low-latency), low (background). Shedding begins at <15% tokens and ramps by priority tiers
Fallback model variants used during shedding (quantized/fast model) are selected via model compatibility matrix in Catalog service
Rollbacks: routing config versioning + immediate global kill-switch in Console integrated with incident automation
rollout_plan: Day 0: Merge behind feature flag. Day 1-3: Internal canary (5% of internal traffic); monitor selected_rate, p95 by region, shed_rate. Day 4-7: Gradual ramp to 25% production traffic for low-risk routes. Day 8-14: 50% + expand to P1 routes. Gates: no p95 regression >5% relative, shed_rate below threshold for high-priority routes. Emergency rollback on breach triggers immediate feature-flag off and circuit-breaker freeze.
notes_summary: This initiative balances latency SLOs against capacity constraints with a combined approach: prefer low-latency local region when capacity exists; gracefully failover using circuit breakers; shed low-value traffic when tokens are scarce; and surface telemetry and guardrails to operations. The design aims for minimal customer-visible disruptions and clear operational controls.
